newsitem.title: USA: LDC DEBT TRAILS T-BONDS, ECUADOR TO ISSUE EUROBOND.
newsitem.headline: LDC DEBT TRAILS T-BONDS, ECUADOR TO ISSUE EUROBOND.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices edged higher Tuesday on the trail of a turbulent U.S. Treasury market, traders said.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. T-bond stormed higher but then faltered, losing ground and taking the Brady bond market along for the ride.

"We saw most of the (Brady bond) buying at the top of the day, which leads me to believe these guys are reluctant investors into the market," one Brady bond trader. "If the U.S. bond market comes off, they don't want to buy (Bradys). If the U.S. bond market goes up, they have to buy."

Spreads of the major Latin benchmarks were little changed. Argentine FRBs slipped 1/8 to 85-1/2 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds picked up 1/8 to 72-5/8. At 1626 EST/2126 GMT the T-bond stood 7/32 lower to yield 6.44 percent.
"I don't think there is much downside risk," Olivier Lemaigre, debt strategist at Citicorp Securities, said. "We should stabilize a bit, especially with Thanksgiving coming."
U.S. financial markets would be closed Thursday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Gary Evans, senior debt strategist at Lehman Brothers, said the bull trend was in place and would persist as long as U.S. markets retain their strength.
"I think we're in fine shape," Evans said. "The smart money is going to try to get in front of the allocation that will come into the market in January."

Elsewhere, an Ecuador Finance Ministry official said the country would launch an inaugural Eurobond in eight weeks. the source said the 400 million bond would have a five-year duration, a price 350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Market talk pegged the price toward the lower end of a 350-390 basis points range because Ecuador was not rated by major credit agencies and the bond size was large compared with the economy as a whole.
Ecuadorean Bradys gave back some of their Monday gains as PDI bonds dropped 1-3/8 to 59-1/4, discount bonds slipped 1/2 to 68-3/4 and par bonds lost 5/8 to 46-7/8.
"There some signs of profit taking on some of the assets that had moved up yesterday," Lemaigre said. -- George Lerner, 212-859-1671
